newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate seen at 10.53-poll.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate seen at 10.53-poll.

text.p: The Philippine benchmark 91-day Treasury bill is seen rising to 10.53 percent at the regular auction on Monday from the previous week's 10.392, a Reuters poll of six financial institutions showed on Friday.
Treasury bill rates are expected to be higher after the Central Bank raised on Friday its overnight borrowing rate by 0.25-percentage points to 10.25.
The 182-day T-bill rate was seen moving up to 10.96 percent from 10.726; and the 364-day to 11.59 from 11.396.
Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza earlier told Reuters the increase in borrowing rates was aimed at aligning it with the rising trend in T-bill rates.
"We just want to realign it with the rates. The T-bill rates had been going up," he said.
The attack on the peso in recent days prompted the Central Bank to take decision action, dealers said.
The foreign exchange market had been jittery due to talk the Philippines may soon be another Thailand where a slump in the property sector affected banks.
The equities market had also been battered as a result of this comparison with Thailand.
On Thursday, the Central Bank had to unload over $100 million to inject calm into the foreign exchange market, dealers said.
"We saw some arbitrage funds leaving because they were not comfortable with the market," a foreign bank trader said.
"Investors are jittery. If interest differentials do not justify the risk, they will go out," another trader said.
